title: Train taste as a filter
principle: Taste is curated judgment: collect references, articulate why they work, and use that filter to reject average options early—not after polish.
procedure: Collect 10 references you respect; write one sentence why each works.
Apply the filter to first drafts: kill anything that fails the rules.
Update the filter when a project teaches a new why.
Keep the filter personal and specific—avoid generic ‘clean modern’.
examplePrompts:
Build a taste filter for this project.

10 references with one-sentence whys.
3 rules we will obey.
List of defaults we will reject on sight.
Do not output a generic mood board without rules.
tips: van Schneider’s public writing emphasizes personal taste and process.
